describe: Was sold a promise that to go to college, follow dreams and start a family would all be easy in America. Even though I have accomplished that, I have had to sacrifice a lot more than previous generations while not getting to enjoy life as much as we should.

I do not feel left behind at all. I have had opportunities in my life to work hard and to succeed in whatever I would like to do. My setbacks have been of my own making and mistakes I have made along the way. I am blessed to be living in the greatest country in the world where opportunities are there if you want to try.

Sometimes I feel left behind in terms of wealth.  We are doing well but there are people that have invested well and are very wealthy.  I feel left behind by some of those people honestly.  But I'm grateful for what I have and don't complain at all.
I do not feel behind at all and I don't understand why I would. I have the same opportunities as everyone else

I was raised by a lower class family. I did not grow up with a college fund, I was never given a car by my family, wedding funds, or help with down payments for a home. I had to rely on myself to get myself where I am today. I feel like others have been given a lot more of a head start in life.

I feel like I am discriminated for being a man. There's no interest that represents me out there. Even TV shows think I'm stupid and incompetent (see dumb husband commercials). Universities hate me (see college enrollment rates by gender). The entire world hates me for existing.

In our society there is always a hierarchy or top corporate people who are advanced and ahead while people at the bottom are at disadvantage quite often. I relate to being disadvantaged therefore I feel left behind but that is why hard work and dedication goes far.
I am a person of color and there's inherent issues that come with it that make me feel out of the loop. But I'm also privileged in other ways so I'm not completely left behind
The main reason is that I need to get a better job and build wealth for the future. Get a wife and house and children and all that, but it begins with getting a decent job.

I feel like I have gotten the things in life that I want, but I feel like it took me a lot longer to get them than it should have. So, I feel somewhat left behind even if I got to where I needed to be if that makes sense.

I just feel like I'm not making enough money, I'm not doing enough by not starting a family (I don't want kids) when all of my other friends are having kids, I still struggle with money, i still want to do things that are childish.

Because I have not achieved similar things that others in my age-range have achieved. While everyone else is having kids, getting married, buying their first house, etc. I'm just doing the same things I was doing back when I was in my early twenties.
Sometimes I feel like I’m not where I should be in life. And that I am not as financially set as I should be.
I sometimes feel like my peers are advancing while I am not. Given technology and how fast things are changing, I worry I may be a bit left behind.
Technology is advancing so quickly that one can certainly feel left behind especially the older generations.

I don't feel left behind at all. I work hard for what I earn and have always tried to improve my standing in the world. I don't rely on others to "carry me forward" so I can't be left behind. What happens to me is up to me.

I honestly cannot think of any way I could be left behind.  I set goals and work hard to accomplish them.  My life is not perfect but I'm pretty satisfied where i am and have goals to progress further.
I can't afford the latest gadgets and cars. I drive an old car and don't have smart appliances. I feel like I'm falling behind on the modern lifestyle.
I had never stayed on the same track as most peers when it came to furthering education and job prospects. As a result, I feel behind financially
I feel a little left behind due to the choices I have made in my life.  But not to a great extent. There are others that are probably feeling this more.

I feel left behind in the career and wage earning walk of life. I just feel like I should be earning and doing more with my life. It's pretty stressful to be honest and sometimes I just feel like i'm not really making much progress towards my goals.
I feel it's very difficult to get employed, it takes so many resources just for a minimal job that doesn't pay nearly as much as you need it to.

I feel left behind because of the healthcare industry, specifically the ridiculous costs. Health insurance is incredibly expensive, and on top of that many times it does not even pay for what you need it to pay for. There is obviously some incredibly fishy things going on in healthcare and health insurance, and I feel like this is a pretty specifically U.S. problem that is often ignored because of the large amount of money the industry has to lobby and influence politicians.

I am fortunate to be where I am but everything is becoming more expensive and it doesn't show any sign of slowing down. Combine this with the creep of technology which will automate a lot and I don't see a future where the average person can earn a good living and live an enjoyable life, similar to the one I currently have.
I felt left behind growing up as a foster kid. I do not feel left behind now. I wasnt afforded the same oppurtunities or clothes growing up. Life is beautiful.

I feel behind because it seems like the economic situation is hard for people in the lower middle class. I also feel left behind because older generations seem to have it slightly better than I do. I feel like I should be further along in life sometimes. Or that I thought I would have made it further by now. Thanks.
I feel left behind when it comes to being about to find affordable housing for my family. Rent is unrealistically high and buying a home is so complicated and expensive.

I feel a bit left behind in that I am in my mid 30s and I am still unmarried and childless. Seemingly most of my peers are married and raising young children, while I am still navigating the hellscape of modern dating. In this way, I feel hopelessly left behind.

It sometimes feels if I have been left out of a large amount of things. I feel out of place. Like I belong to a different era. The world is rapidly changing and not for the good. Too many weird ideas being foced upon people by the small, vocal minority.

I feel that the elite are taking from everyone and doing all they can to leave us behind. The current administration is leaving everyone behind they can while filling their coffers. People are becoming more hateful due to the administration. They are purposely destroying our economy to make us poorer.
feedback: I hope you collect the data needed to complete your research.

describe: I don't really feel left behind by the economy or anything like that. I'm starting to feel left behind by age and ageism. I'm 70 and retired. I thought about getting a small part time job just for a little extra cash and looked into several possible opportunities but none of them panned out basically because of my age. A few people actually said it out loud. The other thing about age is losing family members and friends. My parents and siblings have all passed away and about 65% of my high school classmates are dead. Many people I worked with in my career are dead. Many of the people I served with in the US Air Force are dead. Honestly, it's starting to get a bit lonely and you do start to feel left behind. It seems difficult to make new friends at my age.

I actually don't really feel left behind at all. I feel like I come from a very privileged position. I think perhaps the only way I maybe feel left behind is that I went to public school in a state that does not value education.

I feel left behind on the relationship level and career. Currently single after 2 divorces and I am still struggling with coming up with successful business plan. I always wanted to work for myself and I feel like I have not found my calling yet.
In general, I do not feel left behind. The only exception is that sometimes I feel trivialized as An older adult, which may result in me being passed over or ignored for certain opportunities.

I was born into a very poor family. Financially I have always struggled. I’m in my 40s and just now understanding the importance of investing. I never had children, or a wife. I spent so much of my early adulthood trying to pull myself out of poverty it just never came for me. I feel behind all my friends and coworkers in every way. I’ve had to come to the realization I will never have some things because of where I started. And most of it was just learning basic things I could have learned as a teenager but had nobody to teach me. I’m left playing catch-up with finances and all other aspects.

I feel a bit left behind because I am currently married, have 2 children, but we still are renting a house. We are unable to afford buying a house yet, and I see classmates getting married and buying a house next. I feel behind in homeownership.

I do not feel left behind at all. I think that it's up to me to try to fit in wherever I am. I should not look at other people and compare myself to them. I think that people find happiness in themselves and their circumstances. It can be a beautiful peaceful thing.
My 20s went poorly and now im just sort of ten years behind. Bad social skills, no family, etc. It wouldnt bother me if it werent for societal expectations and judgements surrounding people my age
i think because of the way people keep getting richer and the other people there income doesnt improve

I feel that as a millennial I never really caught much of a break. I graduated with student loan debt into a bad economy, was under-employed for years, and then when I finally did get a good paying W-2 job the work ended a few years later due to funding issues. I worry about saving for retirement and taking care of my parents in the future.

I feel left behind in the world of technology.  Most importantly, when it comes to entertainment.  For example, I really want to get into VR/AR.  In fact, Android is debuting their XR glasses very soon, and I would love to get me and my wife those.  But I simply just can't afford it.  Even those headsets that apple came out with look extremely cool, and would be fun to have.  But at the end of the day, I just can't swing it.  And just simply not having enough money leads to other feelings of being left behind also.  I want to travel, plan for my future, etc.  But that's hard to do when every last bit of your paycheck goes to just breaking even. So  to sum it up, I wish I could change my answer to the previous question about how much I feel left behind, because now that I think about it, I would have rated that a lot higher on that sliding scale.

As you age, you seem to be sort of discriminated against most job opportunities.  I have held many high-profile positions during my career.  The company that I worked at in my last job, ended up closing the location that I worked at.  Being over 65 years old, most place of employment are not willing to bring someone on at my age.  I feel I still have lots to offer and many more year to work.  That is one way of feeling left out or behind.  Additionally, most of my close friends have passed away, leaving me with very few (almost none), close friends, making me feel somewhat left behins.
Left behind to me means that I am not advancing in my career. Also means that I either don’t have savings and/or don’t have a house I own.
maynbe i feel some people are ahead of me financially. im kinda of nbehind in my career path. I feel i am behind in advancing and also fee lbehind in having kids. im already 34!

I'm white and in the middle class so, most of the time, I haven't felt "left behind".  There was a time in the 1980's when I was entering the corporate world as a woman and faced some challenges because most of my co-workers were men.  When I was a stay at home mom I felt a bit left behind because the expectation by my family and society was that I would work full-time.  Recently,  I feel a bit left behind because I'm a Strong Democrat and very liberal. This country is run by a Far Right President so many of the things happening in this country are very against my values.

To feel left behind means that you feel that people are not listening to your needs/desires as they do with others that are higher in social status and wealth.  You are thought less of, discriminated against, treated differently, don't have access to things that others are.
As a senior and veteran living on Social security, I feel left behind a bit because I make just over the minimum for some financial help from the government.

I think economically I feel a little behind. I'm in my early 40s and I've been working since I was 18 and I don't think I'm where I want to be financially. I think I'll be fine in the long run, but I wish I was a little better off because a major catastrophe could lag me behind my financial goals.
I feel like the economy is set up where the working class is not meant to level up because as the prices of living our rising the pay doesn’t increase by much and it leaves us stressed about finances
I recently moved to a new area so i don't get to see too many familiar people very often. When i get a chance to see old friends I have a lot to catch up on.
There are just things that I am used to and from my past that just aren't around anymore. It makes me sad that those ideals are just left behind and no one cares about them anymore.

I grew up in a very disfunctional family, and we did not have the benefits normally expected by traditional families.  We were the children of the town drunk and were on the very bottom rungs socially.  Consequently, we were not included in much of what was conssidered "normal" American society.   We did not and were not expected to go to college, have good jobs, decent places to live....my siblings and I decided that socially we were even lower on the success ladder than migrant workers and were by and large ignored or  reviled by other segments.
feedback: Yes...thank you very much for including the choice of "neither" in the question do you consider yourself more democrat or republican.  Too many times I have answered this question knowing I would have to select one or the other, knowing that i espouse neither ideology...I have always been independent...trying to learn about the issues and the candidates regardless of their political loyalties.  I believe that should be the guiding light for anyone serious about trying to make the country better, or at least not worse.

describe: As a college student, I feel like the debt I have accrued will only screw me over long term. No one is coming to help me either. All loan forgiveness is bullshit and won't happen.

I lost touch with a lot of my friends, so this was the first thing that came to mind. I have not tried to contact any of them for a long time. This is the main reason I would feel left behind. In reality, I do not. This is just an illusion I believe.
Well, I moved the slider to the "I don't feel left behind" side. Unsure what you mean by "left behind"?
I feel like every one else is getting ahead and I'm not. I'm not making as much money as everyone else, and my views are becoming more and more rare.

I live in a small town that has seen better days. It is struggling economically, and we lack high quality education and health care services. When I travel to larger cities, the difference in progress is often staggering.

Well as I get older I find it really easy and anybody that gets older can tell you that you start to get left behind by everything and everybody job opportunities dry up friends disappear your children don't talk to you it's yeah it's a feeling of being left behind by society in general

I am a white, straight, male, aged 65+. I grew up in a household that made sacrifices to send me to college and graduate school. As such, I've been privileged beyond most all of my peers. I'm sure that I have benefited from my birth circumstances far more than I even realize. So, I don't feel left behind almost at all - I've made something out of the many advantages I've had in life. If there is ANY way that I possibly feel "left behind" - then it might be some instances of "ageism" that I feel I've observed since I turned 62. Some few opportunities that were open to me at a younger age seem to have become rarer once I got well into my sixties.
feedback: You noted the term "liberalism" as one of your ideologies. That word can have multiple meanings (e.g. "classical" liberalism or modern day label of "liberal"), so I chose NA for that particular question.

describe: I was born left behind. The plan was for me to end up in prison and dead as soon as possible. This was an FBI plan, not just for me, but for millions..
feedback: Thank You for the opportunity to participate!

describe: As a senior citizen, I feel that most don't feel that we need to be forward in our thinking and advance our knowledge of technology. I feel that most perceive senior citizens as old and unintelligible when it comes to any new development in technology. They ignore our needs and feel that we do not add anything to society. I find that my experience over the years can add a lot to today's world. I know what works and what does not in many cases. When technology has flaws because it is not user friendly, I can certainly aid in the development of it so that it can be used by all.

I have not exactly been successful in my life. I had a career but had to quit because of an injury. Now I am trying to get back to myself to do something with my life before it is too late. I feel left behind because all of my friends and family are doing much more than me. It hurts really bad because I still have so much to do and want to do.
I am physically disabled and don't live the typical life as other adults. I can't live where I want to, I cant work like I want to. I feel behind compared to my peers, even though its not by choice.

I feel left behind because the rich keep getting richer and the poor keep getting poorer in this country. I feel like all the people at the top have the most money and power and they control everything even though their percentage in the population is much smaller. People are struggling to afford basic necessities and the american dream feels like a myth.
I feel left behind because I highly suspect that my vote doesn't matter in The US.  I feel like the elections are rigged by trump and Musk.  I feel helpless.

I am getting on the older side of things (52) and I am beginning to feel the way my grandparents felt the first time they saw a computer.  I am drawing back on the experiences that formed me 20 years ago and I now am starting to feel what they were probably feeling, that the world was passing me by.  I am looking at students that routinely use AI for assignments and get upset when I fail them for not having a single thought of their own written down.  The things that I was taught that you did and did not do (plagiarism, etc.) just don't seem to matter as much and I am feeling a bit like a relic of the past and am very uncertain about the future.
feedback: What's the importance of the color question?  Was there an attention check I missed?

describe: I am a disabled person. While I am employed and have a home life, the rest of the world seems to disregard me. The opportunity to live a normal life in line with others just isn't possible. I watch as others carry on to fulfilling experiences while I struggle.

I feel that I am not really left behind.  As a white male, I seem to get many benefits of the doubt in life.  I do think that with some diversity efforts it has hurt white males a bit.  However given the benefits, I have gotten in life I can not complain.

I think the way I feel left behind is when I go to make a purchase of a car. The prices have gone up so much that I feel that I can not afford to purchase a good quality car because my pay is lower than people doing the same job as I am. So I feel that if I made more money like counterparts do I could afford to make that purchase without worry.

I don't have a solid and defined career like many people my age do. I don't have children, which is a personal choice. This is a positive thing for me, but I feel "left behind" in some way. I can not drive because I have epilepsy so I lack some independence that the average person my age has.

I feel left behind in my personal life. Most of my same aged friends are married and have children. I do not necessarily want those things currently, but I feel as if they are ahead of me in that regard.

I have had a rough three years after being completely flooded by a hurricane in 2022 and partially flooded by hurricanes in 2024. Having to rebuild my house multiple times in three years really takes a toll on my mental health and I feel like this is not something many people can truly comprehend and empathize. I often feel isolated in my feelings and left out of things going on in the world today because I am focused on putting the pieces back together in my life.

I enjoy living a lifestyle from excessive work or money-making by living in my car. However, with all the recent laws passed and focus on houseless and other transient people, I feel I'm not so much being left behind as much as actively prosecuted
I just think that the price of everything is rising, yet wages are not being raised enough. My husband and I do well, but still don’t have the financial freedom to do everything I’d like to do.
feedback: Nothing that I can think of.

describe:
I've always felt a little behind and never knew why. I'm an intelligent person; I have a degree in Business and another in Law. Yet I never seem to fit in or succeed like others. I'm smart but I've never made it out of poverty. I've always been a manager, yet in nearly 40 years I never made it to District Manager. I'm a really nice person, yet I've never been popular or had a lot of friends. 

Left behind in so many ways for reasons that I couldn't fathom. Turns out, I'm autistic. And I have ADHD, which just amplifies the autism. Autism explains why I am the way I am. Why I always seem to miss out on the opportunities. Why society just doesn't make any damn sense.

I feel like I'm lagging behind everyone in my social circle. They have advanced in their careers and are going on multiple holidays every year and investing in real estate, whereas I feel like I stagnated years ago, and every year is like Groundhog Day. Since my cancer diagnosis, I feel lost; it's like I forgot how to live, and the world has just been speeding by me. I'm standing, watching everyone else have fun, whilst I grind away at the same position within the same company for the past 10 years. I've lost touch with close friends, and family members appear more distant.
I feel that that I wasn't allowed to live my life in a way that would allow me to be happy now or have the financial security that would allow me not to fear the future.

Since I became a senior citizen and went on Medicare, I can see that American society does not value the elderly, and would prefer they die as soon as possible.  They would like to siphon all of your accumulated wealth before you go, but after they have all of it, die quickly.
feedback: The current administration is breaking new ground in concentrating power in the executive branch that must be used for good by the Democratic party when they gain power, which will be very soon.  American's won't accept a corrupt, evil  authoritarian regime that is only interested in enriching themselves and their cronies.

describe: I feel as if I'm not very left behind for the most part. In the areas where I do feel left behind, I only feel that way do to my own decisions with career and life choices. Even still, I am pretty satisfied with where I am in life.

I feel left behind since I feel as I have not grown since high school and being in college, I feel the same as I was when I was a freshman. I don't find myself evolving like others have done and feel like I am the same person that I was when I was little still.

I feel the current federal government is doing more to make it unsustainable to live by helping accelerate inflation by deregulation and tariffs and doing nothing to help the working and lower class of society that need relief from constant price hikes on food, fuel, electricity

A lot of my immediate family has passed away. I do not really have communication with many people. I do not feel like I am far enough in life at my age as I should be. I feel like I am not experiencing what I should, and like I am missing out on life.

it seems like most of the people i grew up with are better off than i am. I tend to make the same mistakes and i hold myself back do to poor decicions. I dont have the same goals and i tend to get caught up in the anxioity.
feedback: nope i just hope i wrote long enough

describe: I don't really feel left behind most of the time but I do feel a bit left behind in how my peers have started raising families and have a better grasp on child-rearing than I do.

I feel economically left behind in that many of the opportunities that were accessible to past generations are substantially greater for people my age.  Owning a home especially is a dream I have that is far more difficult for me than it ever was for my parents, for example.  Home prices are multiple times more expensive compared to average wages as they were 30 years ago, interest rates have tripled over the past few years, and where I am in my 30s is very different to where my mom was in her 30s (a home owner supporting 3 children).  I also feel left behind politically.  The United States has slid further and further to the right wing over my lifetime, and I have little representation fighting for my views.  Healthcare is out of reach for many, women have less control over their own body and medical rights than they did 10 years ago, education has gone downhill, and I currently live in an oligarchy controlled by idiots with too much money.
I guess I feel a little left behind in saving for retirement and buying stocks.  I don't understand any of it
I am nowhere near where I thought I would be at this point in my life and I'm getting older so I don't know whether or not I'll ever catch up.
I feel that people my age are more accomplished as far as career.  I feel like I haven’t gone as far in my career as I should be.

I really don’t feel very left behind. I have been extremely blessed in my life. The only thing I can think of, is that I am into my 40s now, and I think that as I continue in middle age, I will start to feel like the world doesn’t pay much attention to older people. Everything is so focused on people being young and beautiful, while aging is inevitable .

The main reason that I feel left behind is the level of education, career and financial success that I have had so far. While I am making advances and iprovements in my life and working toward the things that I need to work towards, I still feel that I am rather far away from where I think or where I need to be at this point in my life. I feel that I made many mistakes, particularly in learning new skills and advancing my education, that has put me behind others, particularly in the area of techology and Ai. I am at a point financially where I am playing catchup, rather than being already established and havig learned the additional skills necessary to continue to advance my career and life forwarrd. I also have not achieve my initial relationship and family goals, which has seperated me from many different sub groups of society as a result and given the limited amount of time, along with my responnsabilities, I don't feel that I will likely achieve my initial goals in that area.

I feel left behind because of my financial situation.   I've recently retired and only recieve a small amount each month from SS.  It isn't enough to survive (I was a homemaker/stay at home Mom for many years) but it's too much to qualify for any assistance like food and medical help.   You hear about other people recieving financial, medical, and food assistance but there isn't anything for seniors in my situation.
I really do not feel like I have been left behind. I am a female who had a great career in IT. It was a struggle at the beginning but I never felt left behind.
As a sixty plus year old in the technology industry, it is almost impossible to get work with another company.  Age discrimination in this industry is rampant.

I feel like I'm left behind in two main aspects, income and healthcare. The income gap disparity between the rich and middle class grows every year. With our current political climate, it won't change no matter who is in office.

As regards to healthcare, we have such an ass backwards healthcare system. IT IS NOT THE BEST. We pay per citizen more than double that of 99% of other countries do on healthcare per citizen. Our private insurance system is a scam. The general public wants universal healthcare, but both the democrats and republicans refuse to implement it because they are all bought and paid for. it is disgusting. We are all being left behind.
I feel left behind when it comes to paying off debt quickly. I am lucky to be in upper middle class, but still struggle because money does not go as far.

I don't believe the government or society at large is looking out for me. COVID is a major reason why I feel this way as it shattered my belief in community. Economically life is a struggle and socially life is also a struggle. Due to my medical conditions I still must take COVID and other illnesses seriously, yet nobody is willing to accommodate my needs anymore. The politicization of the pandemic harmed society's ability to feel empathy for others. As such, I feel left behind as society moves towards a new vision that does not have a place for me in it.
I feel like I worked hard all my life, saved hard and yet when I look to my future toward the time when I might need someone to care for me, I realize I will not be able to afford care for myself.

I feel like I missed out on important life experiences thru the years.  I feel incomplete in my life knowlege.  Its the simple day to day things that I struggle with.  I have to struggle on just to try to keep up the pace of life.  A lot of it is personal so this will have to do.
feedback: Im not sure what the color question was for ?

describe: I'm feeling left behind in the sense there are not many good job opportunities for young adults and everything is getting way too expensive with inflation and tariffs
The only time I feel left behind is when I think about the ability to purchase a home. There are people my age who bought homes before prices exploded and now it does not seem very attainable.
I feel that I barely make enough money to support myself.  I sometimes feel that I am left behind in the economic sense, like other people may be able to afford nicer things than I can afford.

At my age, 76. I find myself having a hard time keeping up with the latest technology items. Which leaves me feeling a little left out of the great American experience. The real bummer about this is that I made my living from the exact thing. In fact my masters is in educational technologies.

I am not as far in my career as I'd like to be. I think working from home mades advancement in the workplace more difficult because you have to put in a lot more effort to get in front of the people who would ultimately be responsible for granting promotions and raises.

I feel like given my age and background, I am definitely not where I should be in terms of financial security/career success. I think that my environment has held me back in many ways and I was not confident enough to pursue some of the goals I had. I think that my anxiety/depression held me back and put me behind others. I am barely taking steps now that I should have taken decades ago but it feels like it is too late in some aspects.
feedback: I can't think of anything at the moment. Thank you.

describe: I do not feel left behind. I am very fortunate to live a good life, and it has been mostly by relying on myself and not depending on others. So there's no one to have "left me behind."

The major ways I feel that I am being left behind revolve around how much baby boomers have done to the economy. I don’t know if I will be able to afford buying a house due to stifled wages in the name of continued profits, as most of my generation is facing. I’ll also have to wait to save adequately for retirement as I am still paying off student loans from expensive higher education. Lastly, having children in this economic climate and providing the life we want for them is leaving us strapped for cash between my paychecks.

I feel very left behind in terms of economic success and career development.  I think that my friends are all much better off financially than me.  This makes me feel very far behind and left behind in terms of life quality.
I feel left behind in ways that we handle healthcare in America. Citizens need to have healthcare support and it is essential and I feel the country is leaving us behind in this regard.

Life is getting very hard, I am not of a high pay scale and it's worrisome to know how I am going to continue working a paying my bills.  Food is another factor.  Seems like social media influencers are the only ones making money and becoming like the rich. At my age I can't start over.
I feel like people caring about others are being left behind by the people who only want to think about themselves and not care for others.

I feel left behind in areas of financial security. It feels like things are always going to be expensive and a struggle to pay for due to lack of strong income. It also feels like many people around me are perhaps starting new ventures and going to more places than I am, which makes me feel less experienced in life. There seems to be many times when I see people who are younger or a similar age as me being much more successful and pursuing things with greater success than me.

I feel that because of my age,73, I am left behind because people think that I am old and therefore stupid or have thoughts and opinions that don’t agree with theirs.  My life experiences are discounted as not important and many feel that I and others my age or older have nothing left to add to society.  We should be “put out to pasture” and our knowledge should be ignored.

I feel left behind when it comes to pop culture. I find it harder and harder to get motivated  to try new film tv and music because I am vastly more attached to older stuff. As a result people talk about actors and musicians I never heard of. That makes me feel like I’m truly left behind snd part of an older era.
Now that I'm old, people ignore me, and assume I'm stupid and incompetent. That also makes it more difficult to find a job.
In my age it is hard to find a reasonable health and child care but I see no reasonable assistance in this regard from federal or state governments.

I think an area where I may feel a little left behind is in my family . One of my children is an adult and is now graduated from college and starting her life...her adult life.  It means that while I am still important to her she needs to leave behind being my "child"  I have to let her be an adult now and she has to take that role.

Of course, this is a very vague thing, being "left behind." I suppose that could come down to several factors, most of it having to do with feeling that life hasn't been what you expected it to be. But does that have to do with financial status? Social status? Personal affirmation? It's hard to say. For me, I feel that I have a robust social life, with many friends of many backgrounds. I have a rich family life, full of laughter and love. I have meaningful spiritual life that nourishes my soul daily. So, in general, I don't feel "left behind," yet there is always that nagging feeling that, despite all I've accomplished, I could've done more by this point. I could've published my book. I could've produced more music. I could've joined a touring band. I could've traveled around the globe. I could've become a performer. I could've become a lawyer, or a doctor. I could be much more rich. I could have way more friends. I could've done way more good things for the world. But it's all conjecture. It's all a fruitless thought experiment with little bearing in reality. I choose to stay here, in the present, right where I am with what I'm doing and feeling now. And when I realize that my destiny is in the hands of God, and my only job is to be faithful with what He's given me, then I don't feel left behind. Feeling left behind means looking back with regret; feeling prideful means looking ahead with lustful ambition; feeling hopeful means being faithful in the here and now.

describe: I don’t feel left behind, I don’t really have much opinion on that question. I think that my current low household income level is mainly my and my husband’s own faults plus having to deal with illness and circumstances beyond our control. Very few of my issues are caused by society, except perhaps for unhealthy food and unhealthy living environments that have been caused by greedy companies and greedy government.

I feel that people who are wealthy are never left behind. I think that people in need are not taken care of as they should and are not respected as much as the wealthy. People in need have to jump through hoops jut to get something as essential as healthcare but wealthy people get it most of the time without paying a dime. It is disgraceful in a country so rich that the poor have to suffer

I feel left behind because there isn’t much guidance in my life. Since reaching adulthood I been figuring everything out on my on I don’t have people I can get good advice from to help me make decisions. I’m completely winging it out here in this world and praying for the best
i do not feel left behind as i am able to achieve the basic necessities for myself and also my family and i am so happy i am able to
"Left behind" to me, is in a sense of not connecting well with others, and not keeping up with the trends. I have always felt "out of the loop".
I see many people advancing in all walks of life. I feel stuck in the same city, same job, same everything.
I consider myself in the middle of the pack but where in lagging behind is not educating myself in personal finances while I was younger so now I'm playing catch up to make up for lost time.

I think in comparison to where I wanted to be form where I am makes me feel left behind and I really shouldn’t. I am successful, I have a beautiful family and home, but I thought I’d be more successful in some ways. For example, I thought I’d get a chance to have another baby or I thought we’d have more money saved or I thought I’d be doing better in my career. I also thought my relationship would be in a better place. I think that part is the hardest.

I think my generation specifically feels left behind because we will never be able to afford a home, we compete with older people with much more experience just for a cashier position at McDonalds, our degrees don’t seem to amount to anything when it comes to getting us a job in our field we went to college for.
I would feel excluded when I see that many of my friends have other types of events to attend or simply dont invite me. There I feel that something is happening that motivates me to feel excluded.

I am white and elderly, 69 years old. At this age society has written me off as "has been" rather than as a walking library of experience and knowledge as well as wisdom. First, my age makes me unimportant. Secondly, being white puts me at the back of the line for any support that would make my life easier. Thirdly, i am a US citizen! And, that really puts me at the back of the line for any help. When i look at the current state of affairs, local governments defying federal agencies and inciting violence against ICE to harbor illegals. What planet am i on? I look at how little anyone cares about senior citizens and it is shameful. Seniors receive little consideration from politicians and policy. It is sad. Sad, that illegals get more protection, respect and consideration.

describe: I don't really feel behind but then again I do in certain parts of life but then a then everyone is on a different path in life and a different journey so I understand why they have more than others. I use to sit around and watch their parents give them things such as cars and help they need while mine would never do that. I also watched people buy a house or get an apartment before I could and it just felt unfair because I worked just as hard as they did.

When I observe how rapidly others advance in terms of technology, employment prospects, and financial security in comparison to me, I occasionally feel left behind.  Some people, for instance, appear to progress in their careers more quickly, earn higher salaries, or have access to networks that support their success.  I also observe that, despite my best efforts, it can be more difficult to keep up with the growing expenses of living and the scarcity of opportunities.  When others have greater resources, support networks, or access to healthcare and education, I occasionally feel socially left behind.  It's not that I'm failing; rather, it's that I feel like I'm falling behind despite my best efforts and perseverance because the pace of progress around me seems to be faster than mine.
There are so many thing I want in future and I feel that I might not be able ton achieve them like others are

I was born between two generations-- right before the internet generation. So I feel like had I only  been born a bit later and have had easy access to so much information and education, I would be in a much better financial situation than I am now. Although I make good money and have saved a lot, lack of financial education has kept me one step behind. I started investing late and missed the boat to own a home with low interest rates. I definitely feel left behind.

in terms of finances i can say i am not exactly where i want to be at but not really left behind , i had all these big dreams of how things would go for me in a couple of years, and it didn't go as planned, but I'm still living alright but then again, i know it should have been way better for me right now

To begin with, I do not feel left behind. What I have are challenges. I suppose within these challenges, there are times that I need to resolve them without any outside assistance. In a manner, I may feel "left behind". In fact, I am currently going through one right now where I need to justify certain actions I recently took to other people who are questioning them and are being difficult.
I don't feel left behind.  Nor did I say I did.  I clearly stated I did NOT feel left behind, yet for some dumb reason I have to write 100 characters here.

describe: Sometimes I feel left behind when it comes to how quickly technology and trends change. It seems like others adapt right away, while I need more time to learn and adjust. I also feel this way in my career at times, when I see peers moving ahead faster or achieving milestones I haven’t yet reached. Socially, it can feel like others are more connected or in tune with what’s happening, while I’m still catching up. These moments make me question if I’m moving at the right pace or if I’m missing out on opportunities to grow and keep up.
I don't particularly feel left behind. I've done my best in life to make the right choices and succeed in the ways society and my family expect.
I do not fit in socially and have different political opinions. I often feel left out of groups and friendships.
I don't feel realy left behind. I feel that the social climate in the USA is not as open, nice, and friendly as it was in the 70's and 80's.

Our current government, regardless of what it says, is leaving all of the middle class behind, as well as the classes below it. In fact, there's no rhyme or reason to their approach, other than to make personal money for themselves. Companies are also leaving humanity in general behind, chasing the next great shiny automated object in an effort to increase profit at the expense of people in general.

I don't feel left behind but a few times before in the past I have felt this way it is in the career areas in my life I felt as though a few of my family members have gotten far and beyond me when it comes to training and certifications licenses etc....

I feel society and the education system has often not been built around encouraging creativity, pushing only certain ways of life such as high-discipline careers, university degrees, and so on. The concept of career to define who you are (or at least make you rich) in general is emphasized as the core of fulfillment everyone should be chasing after if they are to be happy. But there are other truths of life I've learned, realizing how much I have buried my right to live a slow life enjoying the simple things, pursuing my creative side even if it is not bringing economic benefit, exploring myself internally instead of just externally to know myself through validation from others. I've always been creative since I was a child, but it wasn't until I turned 30 that I finally decided to let go of my 'career woman' mentality I felt encouraged toward in STEM and to just feel free to find my own way of being productive, self-fulfilled, and contributing to the world, not society's way. I feel left behind by the system in the sense that the system stifles the psychological needs of creativity (open-mindedness, lack of rigidity, play), something that is stomped out of most children from a young age, but for those who maintain their creative mind, they have a tough time making it or being understood.
I think with technology I am not advancing like I used to. Also a bit with things like cryptocurrency
I'm not left behind, it's just that I have lofty goals. I'm not competing with anyone, I'm creating, so it's not accurate to say that I feel left behind.

I dont feel extremely left behind but I do notice moments where I feel somewhat outpaced especially in areas like rapid technological changes. I sometimes feel behind in how quickly others adopt these things and theres almost a subtle pressure.

The only way I’d really feel left behind is being bi sexual. I feel like I don’t really completely fit on either side. Judged by people who are lesbian and also not straight. So in that aspect I can feel a bit left behind.

not really left behind just feel stuck now so I feel it coming over time. I just don't believe in this place anymore so what is the point of working for it. I will just use my energy to get by and not stress too much about the time remaining. It is a crazy world out there

I feel left behind because it is a struggle to pay for the basics with rent and utilities so high. The system is set up where the more you make the easier it is because money can make money with investments and interest. Starting at the bottom makes it almost impossible to get to the top.
I don't really. I just don't always feel seen as a female with mental health struggles. I also am aging and some things just don't came as quickly like technology.

It seems to me that this country has chosen to only support the "Haves" while leaving those of us in the "Have-nots" group behind. You must be rich to do anything in this country, and participation in any of its processes seems only for those who have the financial means to do so.

Though I am perfectly comfortable with the progress I have made in my life, I would only point to family-raising as the area where I feel left behind. Now their children are married and have had grandchildren, but my first is even yet to marry.

Although I have obtained and accomplished most of my desired goals.I feel like there is still a very small part of life missing. On average I feel like I'm equally compared to people my age, yet there is still much to be desired.

describe: If I were left behind in anything, it would be mainly due to my age. Having 5 children and limited income, has set us up, my husband and I, for a scary retirement. We have some retirement, but it would only last a few years. We are forced to keep working, and I am not sure how much longer my husband can work full time
I feel left behind because I already started behind, aka was not born into wealth. But as the income gap grows larger, far more more people are being left behind so I have a lot more company.

I wouldn't really say that I feel left behind. when thinking about it though, I guess in a way the only way I feel behind would be seeing everyone around me moving, doing things, always something happening and like I cant keep up with it. sometimes when I think of the fact that time is fluid, it makes me feel like I cant keep up with the pace of time and life

I feel a little left behind because of my age and the fact that I am disabled. As I get older I am not able to participate in activities that I did when I was younger. For most of my life I was extremely fit and able to do a wide variety of physical activities. Now, as I get older and as I experience a recent disability, I am left behind. I can't run. I cannot dance, I am limited in yoga, and I walk slower. These are primarily caused by my disability as even five years ago I could do most of these activities.
I'm retired and very dependent on Gov. to send SS monies. I do have some other monies that I use, but am primarily dependent on SS.

I sometimes feel left behind in relation to the rapid pace of technological change and the rising cost of living. The constant evolution of tools and systems in the workplace makes it difficult to stay fully up to date. At the same time housing healthcare and education have become increasingly difficult to afford compared to what earlier generations experienced. This creates the sense that no matter how much effort one puts forth it is challenging to achieve long term stability. Opportunities also appear unevenly distributed with some individuals having access to better schools networks and resources while others struggle without similar support. Although I do not feel entirely left behind I am aware of widening gaps in certain areas which can at times feel discouraging.
I feel like I am catching up with the changes happening. I think that economic and social factors influence how I feel.

I feel like I have not necessarily received what I deserve from what I interpret to be the social contact we have in our society. I feel like I did the things that I was told to do, but I didn't necessarily get I was owed. I feel like I am not very prepared to exist in society as it is nowadays.

I feel left behind because of my economic upbringing. People with money have more chances in life and guidance. My family isn't as economically stable or educated. I didn't make choices that were in my best interest because of the lack in knowledge at the time and poor guidance from my uneducated parents.

I am 56 years old and have worked very hard all my life, but I feel like now I am experiencing set backs that are harder to come back from. One step forward and two steps back as they say. You try to do the right thing...loyalty to the company and work hard, you just end up getting laid off and have to start over...have kids, save for the future...one has a disability and all the savings goes toward medical costs. Divorce, there goes more savings. It feels to late to go back and get another degree and it is harder to get hired the older you get. It just feels discouraging to try to advance at middle age.

Socially, financially and in general, overall. I seem to be lacking in most areas that others have excelled in over recent years, in spite of the pandemic derailing most for a period of time, I never recovered.

I'm a white male so from that standpoint this country is not leaving me behind. However, it feels like it is headed in a direction I don't want to follow. So much hate and division coming from our own government, it makes it hard to live here at times.

I largely did everything "right" in terms of growing up. I focused on academics, stayed out of trouble, went to a good college, and interned at a respectable company. However, after graduating I just couldn't get a full time job in a relevant field. It's been so long now after graduation that I feel like I've lost all desirability in terms of being hired. I'm watching everyone else have fulfilling careers, while I'm just floundering, barely making ends meet.

I sometimes feel powerless like I don't have a voice.  I know that many people are struggling but it doesn't make my own struggles any easier.  I feel like I don't have as many opportunities as I imagined in life when I was younger.
being white means many things are explicitly designed to disadvantage me and my descendants. actually, implicitly as well.
